```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
source("../src/etl/suppression.R")

div <- yaml::read_yaml("divisions.yml")[[params$division]]
stopifnot(!is.null(div))
# Optional per-entry fields: department_pattern (filter use by department, for a unit that is not a college division),
# faculty, unit_word. Defaults keep the division briefs unchanged.
faculty   <- div$faculty   %||% paste(div$short, "faculty")
unit_word <- div$unit_word %||% "division"

# DSC activity records matched to a department, from the restricted person spine (2026-10-24 export).
# Aggregates only; cells under 5 are already blank or omitted at export. Not yet in the public claim register.
sp <- read_csv("spine-aggregates-2026-10-24.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
spd <- sp |> filter(division == params$division)
stopifnot(nrow(spd) > 0)
spk <- spd |> filter(row_type == "kind")
spu <- spd |> filter(row_type == "unit") |> arrange(desc(events))
cov <- sp |> filter(row_type == "coverage")
cov_total <- cov$events[cov$item == "ucla_email_events_total"]
cov_unit  <- cov$events[cov$item == "ucla_email_events_with_unit"]
kv  <- function(kind, col) spk[[col]][spk$item == kind]
n_events <- function(kind) { v <- kv(kind, "events"); if (length(v) == 0 || is.na(v)) "fewer than 5" else scales::comma(v) }
n_people <- function(kind) { v <- kv(kind, "people"); if (length(v) == 0 || is.na(v)) "fewer than 5" else as.character(v) }
yrs <- function(kind) { a <- kv(kind, "first_year"); b <- kv(kind, "last_year"); if (a == b) a else paste(a, "to", b) }
unit_rows <- spu |> transmute(Department = item, Records = events)
other_n <- sum(spk$events, na.rm = TRUE) - sum(spu$events)
if (other_n >= 5) unit_rows <- bind_rows(unit_rows, tibble(Department = "Other departments (each fewer than 5)", Records = other_n))

# Staff capacity (claim #17 and the home page)
cap <- read_csv("../data/processed/canonical/service_capacity_by_year.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(fte = dsc_staff_fte + contributed_staff_fte) |> filter(!is.na(fte))
fte_peak <- sprintf("%.1f", max(cap$fte))
fte_now  <- sprintf("%.1f", cap$fte[which.max(cap$year)])
# Doug's wording: "about 30%", not FTE numbers. Rounded to the nearest 5 percent.
fte_drop <- round(100 * (1 - cap$fte[which.max(cap$year)] / max(cap$fte)) / 5) * 5

hl <- read_csv("../data/processed/canonical/headline_aggregates.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
h  <- function(k) hl |> filter(metric_id == k) |> pull(display) |> first()
mon <- function(d) format(as.Date(d), "%b %Y")
at_least <- function(n) if (n < 5) "fewer than 5" else paste("at least", comma(n))
comma <- scales::comma
```

The Data Science Center (DSC) is the UCLA Library team that supports research data, 3D scanning, and data consulting. This brief covers research in `r div$noun` that DSC has worked on and what would help `r faculty`. The research belongs to the faculty and students named; DSC's part is stated each time.

::: {.in-brief}

## In brief

- **What DSC did:** 3D scanning, text recognition, and data hosting for research in `r div$noun`, in the projects below.
- **What is changing:** DSC's staff capacity fell by about `r fte_drop`% between 2022-23 and 2025-26. The Library has announced that drone lending ends this fall and that DataSquad stops running as a coordinated program.
- **What we ask:** a continuity briefing, a named accountable owner, and review milestones. None asks the Library to reverse the reorganization.

:::

## What would help

This work still needs someone when a unit changes shape. **Who will maintain access, technical support, and stewardship for these functions in `r div$noun`, and with what capacity?** Three things would help:

1. A continuity briefing for `r faculty` on which 3D, data, and repository services continue, who staffs them, and where to ask.
2. A named accountable owner for the methods, preservation, and data workflows that cross Library teams.
3. Review milestones, so the `r unit_word` can see in a few months whether capacity held.

## Research we have worked on

```{r examples, results='asis'}
for (ex in div$examples) {
  cat("::: {.research-entry}\n\n### ", ex$title, "\n\n", ex$text, "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("**DSC's part:** ", ex$supplied, ".", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(ex$link)) cat(" [", ex$link_text %||% "Source", "](", ex$link, ")", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(ex$link2)) cat(" [", ex$link2_text %||% "Source", "](", ex$link2, ")", sep = "")
  cat("\n\n:::\n\n")
}
```

::: {.evidence}

## Evidence

### Documented use by the `r unit_word`

These counts come from DSC's own workshop and consultation records for UCLA people, and cover only records where the department or field of study (self-reported) is known and maps to the `r unit_word`. Of `r scales::comma(cov_total)` records from people with a UCLA email address, `r scales::comma(cov_unit)` (about `r round(100*cov_unit/cov_total)`%) could be matched to any department, so these are floors, not the `r unit_word`'s full use.

- **Consultations:** `r n_events("consult")` consultation records from `r n_people("consult")` people in `r div$short` departments, `r yrs("consult")`.
- **Workshops:** `r n_events("attendance")` attendance records from `r n_people("attendance")` people, `r yrs("attendance")`. Most workshop registration forms after 2021 did not ask for a department, so later attendance often cannot be matched; the fall 2025 series asked for a field of study, which we treat as a department-level self-report (it appears here as "Humanities" in the table).
`r if (!is.null(div$registrations)) paste0("- **Registration forms:** ", div$registrations)`
`r if (!is.null(div$topics)) paste0("- **What they came for:** ", div$topics)`
`r if (!is.null(div$research_data)) paste0("- **Research data:** ", div$research_data)`
`r if (!is.null(div$teaching)) paste0("- **Teaching:** ", div$teaching)`

```{r depts}
knitr::kable(unit_rows, col.names = c("Department (consultations and workshop attendance)", "Records"),
             format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

::: {.table-note}
Departments with fewer than 5 records are combined into one row, or omitted if that row is also under 5.
:::

### Services open to every UCLA researcher

Available to `r div$short` researchers, and not evidence that a particular department used them: UCLA Dataverse, the university's research-data repository (`r h("dataverse_datasets_released")` released datasets, Feb 2026); governed access to restricted data through Redivis, including the national voter file; 3D capture, publication, and hosting on pointcloud.ucla.edu; workshops and consultation (`r h("instruction_sessions_lifetime")` workshop sessions since 2017, and at least `r h("people_reached_confirmed_ucla")` confirmed UCLA researchers reached campus-wide, not broken down by division); and DataSquad, the student consulting team that works on faculty projects.

Figures, definitions, and sources: [Research Enabled by DSC](https://ucla-data-science-center.github.io/dsc-stats-reports/), where each figure has an entry in the site's claim register.

:::
